root_cause: The focus trap's checkKeyNav function lacks a fallback destination node when no tabbable groups are found, allowing browser-default focus movement to escape the trap. In the observed case, focus escaped to the body element when tabbing from the last tabbable node.
repair_strategy: Enhance the else branch in checkKeyNav to provide a destination node by attempting to focus the first focusable node in the first container, or the container itself as a last resort, when fallbackFocus is not set.
expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard focus will remain confined within the dialog when tabbing from the last focusable element, preventing accidental focus loss for keyboard users.
functional_risks: Focusing the container (a non-focusable div) is harmless but unconventional; however, it is preferable to losing focus entirely.
If the first focusable node in the container has tabindex=-1, it may receive focus unexpectedly, but this is a rare fallback scenario.
verification_requirements: Pressing Tab from the close button should move focus to the more button, and pressing Tab again should move focus back to the close button (not escape to the body).
Repeated Tab presses should cycle focus between the close and more buttons without escaping the dialog.
Pressing Escape should close the dialog and return focus to the trigger button.
